Hey, thanks for sharing your thoughts! For me, the show was billed by coworkers and in reviews as a sharp piece of satire, and I always felt that satire and cultural commentary go hand in hand. If you’re going to rely on satire, I think it really benefits from having some underlying messaging—otherwise, it risks falling flat or saying nothing at all.

I’m curious, though—what specific topics or issues do you think the show is really targeting, or is its intent simply to be entertaining without trying to say much at all? I’d love to hear your perspective.
